title: How few clues can a Sudoku have?

probes.question: What is the smallest number of clues a standard Sudoku can have and still have exactly one solution?

image.alt: Flat illustration of a 9 by 9 Sudoku grid with 17 coloured dots standing in for the given clues and the rest of the cells empty.

body.claim: A standard Sudoku with only 16 clues can never have a single unique solution. 17 is the minimum.
body.why: Many puzzles with 17 clues and one solution have been found. A 2014 paper proved, through an exhaustive computer search, that 16 clues can never be enough. There are an enormous number of ways to fill a Sudoku grid.
